content.text:
Removed Python 3.15 from CI and package support classifiers. [VTK lacks a Python 3.15 wheel](https://pypi.org/project/vtk/9.7.1/), so changing PyVista constraints cannot resolve the failure.

Python 3.10–3.14 remain covered. Added a comment explaining when to restore 3.15.

TOML, YAML, and formatting checks passed. CI itself hasn’t been rerun.
How do we make sure that people don't install python 3.15 because we don't support that version? Is there somewhere that caps the python version between the ones tested in CI?
`requires-python` controls which Python versions pip accepts. It currently says `>=3.10`, so removing the classifier didn’t block Python 3.15. I’ll add an upper bound of `<3.15`.

input.input:
text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: /home/maxwell-rosen/postgkyl/pyproject.toml
@@
-requires-python = ">=3.10"
+requires-python = ">=3.10,<3.15"
*** End Patch"));
text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"pre-commit run --files pyproject.toml","max_output_tokens":1000}));

content.text:
Yes—`requires-python` in [pyproject.toml](/home/maxwell-rosen/postgkyl/pyproject.toml:31) enforces this. I changed it to:

```toml
requires-python = ">=3.10,<3.15"
```

Pip will reject this release on Python 3.15 or newer. Classifiers only advertise support; they don’t enforce it.

Checks passed. This takes effect for newly built releases; already published releases retain their existing metadata.
